label: assump:smooth-latent-task
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{assump:smooth-latent-task}
  Tasks are indexed by a parameter $\theta\in{\mathcal{T}}=[0,1]^{d_{\theta}}$, with $d_{\theta}\in\mathbb{N}$ fixed across the model class and independent of $n$, but the sampled $\Theta$ remains latent and $\Pi$ may be any Borel probability measure on ${\mathcal{T}}$.
  Let $g_\theta$ denote the Lebesgue density of $P_\theta$ or $P_\theta^{X,Z}$ in the sample-only or input--output model, respectively. 
  Fix $\beta>0$, $L_{\beta}>1$, $\underline{p}\in(0,1]$, $\beta_{\theta}\in(0,1]$, and $H_{\theta}\in[0,\infty)$.
  The map $(\theta,u)\mapsto g_{\theta}(u)$ is jointly Borel and, for all $\theta,\theta'\in{\mathcal{T}}$,
  \begin{equation*}
    g_{\theta}\in{\mathcal{F}}_{\beta,+}^{d_{\mathrm{stat}}}(L_{\beta},\underline{p}),
    \qquad
    \sup_{u\in[0,1]^{d_{\mathrm{stat}}}}|g_{\theta}(u)-g_{\theta'}(u)|
    \le H_{\theta}\|\theta-\theta'\|_2^{\beta_{\theta}}.
                                          
  \end{equation*}

label: prop:balanced-dsm-identity
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Exact variance-balanced DSM excess-risk identity

title: Proof
body_md:
The standard denoising identity \citep{vincent2011}, multiplied by $\sigma_t$, gives the conditional mean at each fixed $t>0$.
Joint measurability and disintegration under $\varpi_{t_0,T}$ give the asserted identity at $\tau$.
Conditional Jensen and $\xi_{\mathrm{dsm}}\in L^2$ imply $\widetilde{s}^{\star}\in L^2$ and finite risk.
For every finite-risk $s$, the squared-loss Pythagorean identity therefore yields
\begin{align*}
  {\mathcal{R}}_{\mathrm{bDSM}}(s)-{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathrm{bDSM}}(s^{\star})
  &=A_{t_0,T}{\mathbb{E}}\|\widetilde{s}(Z_{\tau},\tau,H_n)
       -\widetilde{s}^{\star}(Z_{\tau},\tau\mid H_n)\|_2^2\\
  &={\mathcal{E}}_{\mathrm{score}}(s),
\end{align*}
where the second equality uses $A_{t_0,T}\varpi_{t_0,T}(t)\sigma_t^2=1$.

label: lem:balanced-score-truncation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Scaled-score bound and truncation error

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{eq:positive-time-score-regularity} and cube support,
\begin{equation*}
  \|\widetilde{s}^{\star}(z,t\mid h)\|_2
  \le\frac{\|z\|_2+\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_{t_0}},
  \qquad t\in[t_0,T].
\end{equation*}
This proves the uniform bound on $\mathcal{G}_n$.
Since $\|Z_0\|_2\le\sqrt{d_z}$ and $\alpha_{\tau},\sigma_{\tau}\le1$, forward noising gives
\begin{equation*}
  \{\|Z_{\tau}\|_2>R_{\mathrm{state},n}\}
  \subseteq
  \{\|\xi\|_2>R_{\mathrm{state},n}-\sqrt{d_z}\},
  \qquad
  \|Z_{\tau}\|_2+\sqrt{d_z}\le\|\xi\|_2+2\sqrt{d_z}.
\end{equation*}
The Gaussian probability proves \cref{eq:transformer-good-event-probability}; its strict bound follows from $R_{\mathrm{state},n}>\sqrt{d_z}$.
Combining the score bound with these inequalities and applying Tonelli proves \cref{eq:derived-score-tail-bound}.
Joint Borel measurability follows from the chosen score version and the fixed clipping set, and Gaussian second moments give finiteness.

label: prop:episode-kl-score-approximation
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Episode-level KL control of integrated score error

title: Proof
body_md:
For densities $g,g'$ on a unit-volume cube with $g'\ge\underline{p}$, $\log u\le u-1$ gives
\begin{equation*}
 \mathrm{KL}(g\|g')\le\int\frac{(g-g')^2}{g'}
 \le\underline{p}^{-1}\|g-g'\|_\infty^2.
\end{equation*}
Set $U_i:=Z_i$ in the sample-only model and $U_i:=(X_i,Z_i)$ in the input--output model. Compare the two joint laws of $(\Theta,U_1,\ldots,U_{n+1})$ with the same prior $\Pi$, using $g_\Theta$ and $g_{\pi_\eta(\Theta)}$ as the conditional example densities.
Tensorization of conditional KL gives a bound $(n+1)H_\theta^2\eta^{2\beta_\theta}/\underline{p}$.
Marginalizing $\Theta$ gives the same bound for the full example sequence.
Reordering that sequence into $(H_n,Z_\star)$ is a measurable bijection under either the sample-only or the input--output prompt model, so it preserves KL.
This proves \cref{eq:integrated-episode-kl} for $\zeta=0$.

Let $Q^{\eta,\mathrm{unif}}_{\mathrm{epi}}$ use the uniform distribution over the same grid.
The weights in \cref{eq:integrated-prior-weights} give the identity
\begin{equation*}
 Q^{\eta,\zeta}_{\mathrm{epi}}
 =\frac{Q^{\eta,0}_{\mathrm{epi}}+\zeta Q^{\eta,\mathrm{unif}}_{\mathrm{epi}}}{1+\zeta}.
\end{equation*}
Its density is at least $(1+\zeta)^{-1}$ times the density of $Q^{\eta,0}_{\mathrm{epi}}$.
Integrating the resulting log-density inequality proves \cref{eq:integrated-episode-kl}.
The KL chain rule at $(H_n,Z_\star)$ proves \cref{eq:integrated-predictive-kl}: the conditional KL is averaged under the original prompt law, and the chain rule also contains a nonnegative KL term for the prompt marginal that can be dropped.

Fix $h$ in a $\mathsf{Law}(H_n)$-full-measure set on which the conditional laws are defined, and write $p_t,q_t$ for the OU-smoothed densities of $P_{0\mid h},Q^{\eta,\zeta}_{0\mid h}$.
Their initial densities on the output cube lie in $[\underline{q}_{\mathrm{out}},\overline{q}_{\mathrm{out}}]$ by \cref{lem:positive-smooth-latent-derived-regularity}.
Hence their ratio after convolution is bounded above and below by positive constants.
For $t\in[t_0,T]$, convolution with the OU kernel gives smooth positive densities with Gaussian tails.
Their spatial derivatives are bounded by Gaussian envelopes times polynomials in $\|z\|$, uniformly on this time interval.
In particular, the score identity from differentiating the kernel gives $\|\nabla\log p_t(z)\|+\|\nabla\log q_t(z)\|\lesssim_{t_0,T,d_z}1+\|z\|$.

Both densities solve $\partial_t p=\Delta p+\nabla\cdot(zp)$.
Differentiating $\int p_t\log(p_t/q_t)$ and integrating by parts therefore gives the relative-entropy dissipation identity
\begin{equation}
 \frac{{\mathrm{d}}}{{\mathrm{d}} t}\mathrm{KL}(p_t\|q_t)
 =-\int p_t\|\nabla\log p_t-\nabla\log q_t\|_2^2\,{\mathrm{d}} z.
 \label{eq:ou-relative-entropy-dissipation}
\end{equation}
The drift terms cancel and the coefficient is one for diffusion coefficient $\sqrt{2}$; compare \citet{chengeorgioupavon2016}.
To justify the calculation on ${\mathbb{R}}^{d_z}$, insert smooth cutoffs equal to one on a ball of radius $R$, with first and second derivatives of order $R^{-1}$ and $R^{-2}$, respectively, perform the calculation on their compact support, and let $R\to\infty$.
The bounded density ratio, the score growth bound, and the Gaussian bounds on the derivatives give an integrable upper bound for every differentiated and boundary term, so dominated convergence applies.
Integrating \cref{eq:ou-relative-entropy-dissipation} gives
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t_0}^T\!\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{d_z}} p_t(z)
 \|s^\star(z,t\mid h)-s^{\eta,\zeta}(z,t\mid h)\|_2^2\,{\mathrm{d}} z\,{\mathrm{d}} t
 &=\mathrm{KL}(p_{t_0}\|q_{t_0})-\mathrm{KL}(p_T\|q_T)\\
 &\le\mathrm{KL}(P_{0\mid h}\|Q^{\eta,\zeta}_{0\mid h}),
\end{align*}
where the last inequality uses nonnegativity and contraction of KL under the OU kernel.
Tonelli's theorem and \cref{eq:integrated-predictive-kl} finish the proof.

label: lem:smooth-latent-four-block-construction
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Four-block Transformer construction

title: Proof
body_md:
All reference matrices are compositions of coordinate projections and injections associated with \cref{eq:smooth-latent-token-block-decomposition}, except for the scalar factors $n$ and $\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}}$ described below.
For block 1, set the active query and key projections to zero, project the context-example values from $\mathsf{V}_{\ell}$, and inject the attention output into $\mathsf{V}_{\mathrm{pool}}$.
The summary mask contains exactly the $n$ context-example rows, so softmax attention returns their mean.
For blocks 2 and 3, the active key set of each latent row is a singleton, so the attention weight is exactly one independently of its logit.
Coordinate projection and injection therefore copy the summary pool and the full query--basis array into the indicated blocks of every latent row.

The fixed map $\mathsf{R}_{3,n}$ projects every selector input onto $[-B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}},B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}]$ and uses the one-hot identifier $e_j$.
For $e\in\{0,1\}$ and $|x|\le B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$, the exact affine--ReLU identity
\begin{equation}
  ex=\operatorname{ReLU}(x)
  -\operatorname{ReLU}(x-B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}e)
  -\operatorname{ReLU}(-x)
  +\operatorname{ReLU}(-x-B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}e)
  \label{eq:appendix-smooth-latent-binary-gate}
\end{equation}
selects one coordinate exactly.
Parallel copies select the $j$th pooled likelihood, query likelihood, scalar basis value, and vector basis value.
An affine output layer then forms \cref{eq:smooth-latent-posterior-logit-update} and writes the resulting $(d_z+2)$-vector into $\mathsf{V}_{\mathrm{lat}}$.
The six one-hot role codes and the same binary-gate identity make these tokenwise coordinate updates shared across rows while leaving all other coordinate blocks unchanged.

For block 4, map the output-token role coordinate to $\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}}e_1$ and map latent token $j$ to $\widehat{\ell}_{j,n}^{\mathrm{post}}e_1$ in key space.
The scaled dot product is therefore exactly $\widehat{\ell}_{j,n}^{\mathrm{post}}$.
Map the remaining latent coordinates to $(\widehat{\mathsf{a}}_j,\widehat{\mathsf{b}}_j)$ and inject the weighted attention output into $\mathsf{V}_{\mathrm{out}}$.
This proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-four-block-output} and every row of \cref{tab:smooth-latent-four-block-construction}.
The null-token value is zero for all four value projections of the constructed network, so unlisted rows receive zero attention updates.
The direct-sum dimensions add to \cref{eq:smooth-latent-explicit-token-width}, and the displayed coefficient bound follows from the coordinate maps, selector threshold, posterior-logit multiplier, and scaling used in the dot product.

label: lem:smooth-latent-time-local-basis
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Time-local OU-basis approximation

title: Proof
body_md:
The covariance calculation in \cref{app:subsubsec:diffusion-feature-regularity}, in particular \cref{eq:appendix-smooth-latent-covariance-identity}, applies on every interval $[a_j,b_j]$ with $\sigma_{t_0}$ replaced by $\sigma_{a_j}$.
Affine time normalization multiplies the time derivative by $h_j^{\mathrm{loc}}/2$.
The denominator has query modulus $H_{q,x}$, whereas the numerator has query modulus at most $R_{\mathrm{bal},n}H_{q,x}$.
Combining these observations with the separate state and time derivatives proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-local-denominator-modulus,eq:smooth-latent-local-numerator-modulus}.

Let $\chi_0,\ldots,\chi_K$ be the continuous piecewise-linear nodal hats on the knots $t_0^{\mathrm{knot}},\ldots,t_K^{\mathrm{knot}}$, restricted to $[t_0,T]$.
They are nonnegative, sum to one, and $\chi_j$ is supported on $[a_j,b_j]$.
Each is an exact affine--ReLU function of the globally normalized time coordinate.
The final interval includes any shorter remaining interval: when $K\ge2$, consecutive knot gaps are at least $t_0$ and $h_j^{\mathrm{loc}}\le7a_j$.
When $K=1$, both supports are the whole interval and normalization cancels $T-t_0$.
Thus the hats and the local coordinates after coordinatewise projection
\begin{equation*}
 u_{t,j}:=
 2\min\{1,\max\{0,(t-a_j)/h_j^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\}-1
\end{equation*}
have coefficients and input Lipschitz constants polynomial in $1+T+t_0^{-1}$ when expressed in the globally normalized input.

Consider one scalar function $f$, with range bound $B:=1+\overline{q}_{\mathrm{out}}+R_{\mathrm{num},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ and desired error $\varepsilon$.
Use $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{a,n}$ for the denominator and $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{b,n}/\sqrt{d_z}$ for each numerator coordinate.
On the $j$th normalized cube, construct the tensor-hat interpolant $I_jf$ from the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-dimensional-holder-relu-approximation}, with error at most $\varepsilon/2$.
Let $H_{f,j,n}$ be $H_{a,j,n}$ for the denominator and $H_{b,j,n}$ for a numerator coordinate.
Its number of grid points is $\lesssim(1+H_{f,j,n}/\varepsilon)^{(d_{\mathrm{stat}}+1)/\beta'}$.
Write its tensor hats as $\psi_{j,r}$ and its nodal coefficients as $c_{j,r}$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
 I f:=\sum_{j,r}c_{j,r}\chi_j(t)\psi_{j,r}(u_x,u_z,u_{t,j})
\end{equation*}
has error at most $\varepsilon/2$: every nonzero $\chi_j$ uses a local interpolant valid at that time, and their weights sum to one.

Let $J_f^{\mathrm{loc}}$ be the total number of these local grid points.
Each product $\chi_j\psi_{j,r}$ has $d_{\mathrm{stat}}+2$ bounded univariate factors.
Use the fixed multiplication paths in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-dimensional-holder-relu-approximation} and project their outputs onto $[0,1]$.
Approximate each product to accuracy $\varepsilon/\{2J_f^{\mathrm{loc}}(B\vee1)\}$.
The accumulated error after weighting by the interpolant coefficients is at most $\varepsilon/2$.
Only $c_{j,r}$ vary, and the final coordinatewise projections cannot increase error.
The number of coefficients and operations is $\lesssim J_f^{\mathrm{loc}}\log^2(2+J_f^{\mathrm{loc}} B/\varepsilon)$.
Summing the coordinates and latent-grid points gives \cref{eq:smooth-latent-time-local-basis-size} after absorbing fixed dimension factors.

For arbitrary trainable coefficients, every approximate hat remains in $[0,1]$, so parameter sensitivity is at most $J_f^{\mathrm{loc}}$ before the final nonexpansive projection.
The univariate hat slopes and time-coordinate maps have polynomial bounds.
The multiplication paths have fixed width, bounded weights, and logarithmic depth; their input Lipschitz constants are therefore polynomial in the displayed quantities, by the same layerwise bound used in \cref{eq:fixed-dimensional-holder-parameter-stability}.
Summing $J_f^{\mathrm{loc}}$ paths with bounded output-layer coefficients preserves polynomial input sensitivity.
Running the component networks in parallel and adding inactive coordinates yields the stated common compact parameter cube.
All computations are continuous, so evaluation is jointly Borel and continuous in the parameters.

label: lem:smooth-latent-output-clipping
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Clipping error for the scaled score

label: eq:gaussian-radial-tail-moment
title: Proof
body_md:
The denoising identity gives $\widetilde{s}^{\star}(Z_t,t\mid H_n)=-{\mathbb{E}}[\xi\mid Z_t,H_n]$.
The squared distance to a closed convex ball is convex.
Conditional Jensen therefore bounds its expectation at this conditional mean by ${\mathbb{E}}(\|\xi\|_2-R_{\mathrm{out},n})_{+}^2$.
Integration against $\sigma_t^{-2}{\mathrm{d}} t$ proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-output-clipping-bias}.
More generally, Gaussian norm concentration gives, for every $R\ge\sqrt{d_z}$ and $r=R-\sqrt{d_z}$,
\begin{equation}
 {\mathbb{E}}(\|\xi\|_2-R)_{+}^2
 \le\int_0^\infty 2u e^{-(r+u)^2/2}\,{\mathrm{d}} u
 \le2e^{-r^2/2}.
 \label{eq:gaussian-radial-tail-moment}
\end{equation}
Taking $R=R_{\mathrm{out},n}$ proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-output-clipping-tail}.

label: prop:integrated-transformer-approximation
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Integrated score approximation by the Transformer class

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{eq:regular-grid-floored-score-identity}, the construction in \cref{app:subsubsec:shared-neural-approximation}, in particular \cref{eq:smooth-latent-network-error}, gives an output $f$ before the final radial projection satisfying $\|f-\sigma_t s^{\eta_{\theta,n},\zeta}\|_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net},n}$ on $\mathcal{G}_n$. 
No uniform comparison of $s^{\eta_{\theta,n},\zeta}$ with $s^\star$ is used here.
Recall that $\widetilde{s}^\star=\sigma_t s^\star$, and let $\mathsf{P}$ be radial projection onto the ball of radius $R_{\mathrm{out},n}$.
On $\mathcal{G}_n$, nonexpansiveness and two applications of the squared triangle inequality give
\begin{equation*}
 \|\mathsf{P} f-\widetilde{s}^\star\|_2^2
 \le4\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net},n}^2
   +4\sigma_t^2\|s^{\eta_{\theta,n},\zeta}-s^\star\|_2^2
   +2\|\mathsf{P}\widetilde{s}^\star-\widetilde{s}^\star\|_2^2.
\end{equation*}
Integrate against $\sigma_t^{-2}P_{t\mid H_n}\,{\mathrm{d}} t$ and the original prompt law.
The first term integrates to at most $4A_{t_0,T}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net},n}^2$, the second is bounded by \cref{eq:integrated-latent-score-bound}, and the third by \cref{lem:smooth-latent-output-clipping}.
On $\mathcal{G}_n^c$, use $\|\mathsf{P} f-\widetilde{s}^\star\|^2\le2R_{\mathrm{out},n}^2+2\|\widetilde{s}^\star\|^2$ and the two bounds in \cref{lem:balanced-score-truncation}.
This proves \cref{eq:integrated-transformer-approximation}.

label: lem:smooth-latent-four-block-sensitivity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Token bounds and parameter sensitivity of the four-attention-block network

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Work under \cref{assump:smooth-latent-task}, with the constants given in \cref{lem:positive-smooth-latent-derived-regularity}.
We first count the coefficients and operations in the attention blocks and component networks.
We then use parameter sensitivity to obtain a covering bound and a measurable ERM, while tracking the dependence on the declared grid and component tolerances.

\textbf{Model size and forward-pass cost.}
Exclude the component encoders and the fixed ratio readout, but include every nonzero fixed or trainable scalar coefficient in the four attention blocks and their coordinate-update maps.
The four-attention-block network above can be stored using at most
\begin{equation}
  16(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2+C_{d_z}d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}
  \le C_{d_z}(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2
  \label{eq:smooth-latent-update-storage-bound}
\end{equation}
such coefficients and evaluated using at most
\begin{equation}
  C_{d_z}(n+J_{\theta,n}+4)(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2
  \label{eq:smooth-latent-update-operation-bound}
\end{equation}
sparse arithmetic operations.
Structural zeros, masks, role labels, latent-cell indices, and their bit encodings are excluded under the counting convention of \cref{prop:smooth-latent-complexity}.
Every fixed coordinate-update coefficient has magnitude at most
\begin{equation}
  1\vee n\vee B_{\mathrm{gate},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}\vee\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}}.
  \label{eq:smooth-latent-update-coefficient-bound}
\end{equation}



Each block has four $d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}\times d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ attention projections, so all four blocks contain at most $16(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2$ nonzero projection coefficients.
The role and block injections, coordinate copies, residual writes, scalar projections, and posterior-logit affine sum use at most $C_{d_z}d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ shared nonzero coefficients.
For the selector, one copy of \cref{eq:appendix-smooth-latent-binary-gate} is used for each of the $J_{\theta,n}$ candidate entries in each of the $d_z+2$ selected likelihood-and-basis coordinates.
It therefore uses at most $C_{d_z}J_{\theta,n}\le C_{d_z}d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ shared nonzero coefficients.
This proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-update-storage-bound}.

For a forward evaluation, the number of operations needed to apply the attention projections in all four blocks is $\lesssim(n+J_{\theta,n}+4)(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2$.
The masks in \cref{tab:smooth-latent-four-block-construction} contain $n+3J_{\theta,n}$ non-null query--key pairs, whose dot products and value aggregation require $\lesssim(n+J_{\theta,n})d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ further operations.
The shared sparse coordinate-update maps require at most $C_{d_z}d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ operations per token row, including the $J_{\theta,n}(d_z+2)$ selector gates on a latent row.
Residual additions and fixed coordinate injections cost $\lesssim(n+J_{\theta,n}+4)d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ operations.
Since $d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}\ge1$, these bounds imply \cref{eq:smooth-latent-update-operation-bound}.
Among the fixed coordinate-update coefficients, only the factor $n$ in the posterior logit and the projection and gate thresholds can exceed one.
The trainable attention coefficients are bounded by $1\vee\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}}$ by the parameter-space definition.
This proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-update-coefficient-bound}.


We now add the component networks to these attention-block counts.
The trainable output-layer coefficients of the context-example log-likelihood, query log-likelihood, and OU-basis networks are bounded, up to a fixed dimension-dependent factor, by
\begin{equation*}
  \mathsf{N}_{\ell,n}^{\mathrm{lat}}
  +\mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{qry},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}
  +\mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{basis},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}.
\end{equation*}
The fixed nonzero internal coefficients of these three network families obey the same bound.
The prior contributes $J_{\theta,n}$ trainable logits.
By \cref{eq:smooth-latent-update-storage-bound}, the fixed selector and coordinate-update networks and the trainable attention matrices contribute $\lesssim(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^2$ nonzero stored coordinates.
The fixed ratio readout contributes at most $\mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{rat},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}$ nonzero stored coordinates.
This proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-trainable-parameter-count,eq:smooth-latent-coefficient-storage}.
Evaluating the shared context-example network $n$ times and the query networks and ratio readout once, and then applying \cref{eq:smooth-latent-update-operation-bound}, proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-forward-cost}.
In particular, only the summary row attends to all $n$ context-example tokens, the two coordinate-copy stages use singleton-key rows, and the output row attends to the $J_{\theta,n}$ latent tokens; no dense quadratic all-token attention matrix is evaluated.

\textbf{Covering numbers and measurable empirical minimization.}
To pass from the parameter count to a covering number, we bound the parameter radius and the sensitivity of the score to its parameters.
The final posterior-attention logit uses the standard $(d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}})^{-1/2}$ scaled dot product, so one fixed query or key coordinate is multiplied by $\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{emb},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}}$; this factor is included in the fixed attention and coordinate-update radius.
By construction, the radii of the parameter-space factors in \cref{def:smooth-latent-score-class} are the component-network parameter radii, the prior-logit radius in \cref{eq:smooth-latent-prior-logit-radius}, and the attention-projection radius containing the reference matrices.
Take $B_{\mathrm{lat},n}$ to be the largest of these radii.
This choice is polynomial in the displayed inputs and $\log(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{floor},n}^{-1})$ by \cref{eq:fixed-dimensional-holder-parameter-stability} and Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth-latent-time-local-basis}.
Because $\mathrm{Proj}_n^{\mathrm{par}}$ is nonexpansive in $\ell_{\infty}$, applying \cref{lem:smooth-latent-four-block-sensitivity} after this projection and setting $\mathsf{Lip}_{\mathrm{lat},n}^{\mathrm{par}}:=\mathsf{Lip}_{\mathrm{out},n}\mathsf{Lip}_{4,n}$ proves the required bound.
This proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-parameter-sensitivity} and makes the claimed polynomial dependence explicit.
A grid contained in the compact trainable-parameter cube proves \cref{eq:smooth-latent-score-cover}.
The resulting finite network is jointly Borel in the data and continuous in its parameters.
                                                                                                                         
Since the parameter cube is a compact metric space and the empirical risk is Borel measurable in the training sample and continuous in the parameter (hence Carath\'eodory), the measurable maximum theorem \citep[Theorem~18.19]{aliprantisborder2006}, applied to the negative empirical risk, yields a Borel-measurable parameter selector whose induced score is an exact empirical-risk minimizer; see also \citet{brownpurves1973}.

name: Conditional early-stopping error bound

title: Proof
body_md:
In the sample-only task family, for almost every prompt $h$, the density of $P_{0 \,|\, h}$ is the posterior mixture of the task densities.
The H\"older ball is convex, so \cref{lem:cube-holder-tv-stopping} applies with the same constant and averaging proves \cref{eq:posterior-predictive-tv-stopping}.

For the input--output task family, condition first on the demonstrations $C_n = c$.
Let
\begin{equation*}
  f_c(x,z):=\int f_{\theta}(x,z)\Pi({\mathrm{d}}\theta\,|\, C_n=c),
  \qquad
  \lambda_c(x):=\int_{{\mathcal{Z}}} f_c(x,z)\,{\mathrm{d}} z.
\end{equation*}
The query has density $\lambda_c$, and where $\lambda_c(x)>0$ the predictive output density is $f_c(x,\cdot)/\lambda_c(x)$.
Let $\mathsf{T}_t^z$ denote unprojected OU evolution in the $z$ coordinate and extend $f_c(x, \cdot)$ by zero outside the cube.
Projection contraction, linearity, and cancellation of the query marginal give
\begin{align*}
 {\mathbb{E}}\!\left[
 {\mathsf{TV}}((\mathrm{Proj}_{{\mathcal{Z}}})_{\#}P_{t \,|\, H_n}, P_{0 \,|\, H_n})
 \,|\, C_n = c\right]
 \le
 \frac{1}{2}\int_{[0, 1]^{d_x}}
 \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^{d_z}}
 \left|\mathsf{T}_t^z f_c(x, z)-f_c(x, z)\right|{\mathrm{d}} z \,{\mathrm{d}} x.
\end{align*}
The proof of \cref{lem:cube-holder-tv-stopping} applies verbatim to each nonnegative subdensity $f_c(x, \cdot)$: its mass and its $z$-H\"older norm are bounded uniformly by a constant depending only on $L_{\beta}$.
Integrating over the unit-volume input cube proves the asserted bound without dividing by a lower bound for $\lambda_c$.

For $U=\phi_{\mathrm{pr}}(H_n)$, both conditional laws are mixtures of their counterparts given $H_n$.
Convexity of TV and the tower property give
\begin{equation*}
 {\mathbb{E}}{\mathsf{TV}}((\mathrm{Proj}_{{\mathcal{Z}}})_\#P_{t\mid U},P_{0\mid U})
 \le{\mathbb{E}}{\mathsf{TV}}((\mathrm{Proj}_{{\mathcal{Z}}})_\#P_{t\mid H_n},P_{0\mid H_n}),
\end{equation*}
proving the claim with conditioning on $U$.

label: lem:exact-reverse-score-dynamics
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exact reverse-score dynamics on a positive-time interval

title: Proof
body_md:
At every positive time, Gaussian convolution makes $p_t(\cdot\,|\, h)$ strictly positive and smooth.
Gaussian differentiation gives \cref{eq:appendix-randomized-grid-score-identities}.
Conditional Jensen proves the score bound.
For $\Sigma_{t,h}:=\mathrm{Cov}(\xi\,|\, Z_t,h)$, one has $\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_{t,h}^2)\le\{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_{t,h})\}^2$ and
\begin{equation*}
  {\mathbb{E}}\{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_{t,h})\}^2
  \le {\mathbb{E}}\|\xi\|_2^4
  =d_z(d_z+2).
\end{equation*}
Since $\|\Sigma_{t,h}-I_{d_z}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2\le\{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_{t,h})\}^2+d_z$, this proves the Hessian bound.
The positive-time diffusion time-reversal identity gives $Y_r\sim P_{b-r\,|\, h}$.
Stop the process when it leaves a compact state set and apply It\^o's formula to $(r,y)\mapsto s_{b-r}^{\star}(y\,|\, h)$.
Differentiating the OU Fokker--Planck equation gives
\begin{equation*}
  \partial_t s_t^{\star}
  =s_t^{\star}+(\nabla s_t^{\star})y
  +\nabla\operatorname{div}s_t^{\star}
  +2(\nabla s_t^{\star})s_t^{\star}.
\end{equation*}
Substitution of the exact reverse drift cancels all finite-variation terms except $-S_r\,{\mathrm{d}} r$, proving \cref{eq:appendix-randomized-grid-score-process} up to the stopping time.
The moment bounds in \cref{eq:appendix-randomized-grid-fisher-hessian}, together with $b-r\ge a$, give the square integrability required to let the localization radii tend to infinity and obtain the identity on the full interval.

label: cor:randomized-grid-update-bound
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:randomized-grid-update-bound}
Fix $\beta>0$ and $L_\beta\ge1$, and consider either the sample-only or the input--output prompt model in \cref{eq:hierarchical-sample,eq:input-output-episode} with any Borel task prior $\Pi$.
Suppose the task laws admit jointly Borel densities $p_\theta(z)$ in the sample-only model or $f_\theta(x,z)$ in the input--output model, with $p_\Theta\in{\mathcal{F}}_\beta^{d_z}(L_\beta)$ or $f_\Theta\in{\mathcal{F}}_\beta^{d_x+d_z}(L_\beta)$, respectively, $\Pi$-almost surely.
Let $T>t_0>0$ with $t_0\le1$, and write $\beta'=\beta\wedge1$.
Suppose the learned score is independent of the test episode and, conditionally on the completed training run, finite-valued and jointly Borel with finite integrated squared score error.
Let $M \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy
\begin{equation*}
  M \ge
  \max\left\{\lceil 2A_{t_0,T}\rceil,
  \left\lceil\frac{A_{t_0,T}}{T-t_0}\right\rceil\right\},
  \qquad
  h_{\mathrm{grid}} := \frac{A_{t_0,T}}{M}.
\end{equation*}
When $T-t_0 \ge 1/2$, as under the parameter choices below for all sufficiently large prompt lengths, the simpler condition $M \ge \lceil 2A_{t_0,T}\rceil$ implies both requirements.
Then the sampler uses at most $M$ reverse updates almost surely, and its output distribution, averaged over the random grid shift, satisfies
\begin{align}
  {\mathbb{E}}{\mathsf{TV}}\left(
  \widehat{P}_{0 \,|\, H_n}^{(M)}, P_{0 \,|\, H_n}\right)
  &\le
  \varepsilon_{\mathrm{init}}(T - A_{t_0,T}/M)
  +\sqrt{\frac{{\mathcal{E}}_{\mathrm{score}}(\widehat{s})}{2}}
  +C_{\mathrm{stop}}t_0^{\beta'/2}
  \nonumber\\
  &\qquad
  +\frac{A_{t_0,T}}{M}\sqrt{\frac{d_z(T-t_0)}{6}}
  +e^{A_{t_0,T}/M}\frac{A_{t_0,T}}{\sqrt{M}}\sqrt{d_z(d_z + 3)}.
  \label{eq:randomized-grid-update-bound}
\end{align}
Here $\widehat{P}_{0 \,|\, h}^{(M)}:=\widehat{P}_{0 \,|\, h}^{\mathrm{grid},A_{t_0,T}/M}$, so the parenthesized argument denotes a bound on the number of updates rather than a grid spacing.
Moreover, there is a constant $0<C_{\mathrm{disc}}=C_{\mathrm{disc}}(d_z)<\infty$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{disc}}\le1$, the displayed conditions on $M$ and $M\ge C_{\mathrm{disc}}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{disc}}^{-2}(A_{t_0,T}+1)^2$ make the sum of the two discretization terms at most $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{disc}}$.
Under the parameter choices used in \cref{eq:main-predictive-sufficient-choices}, $A_{t_0,T}\lesssim\log(e/\varepsilon)$ and $\log(e/\varepsilon)\ge1$, so $A_{t_0,T}+1\lesssim\log(e/\varepsilon)\lesssim\log\varepsilon^{-1}$ for $\varepsilon\le1/2$.
Thus, for a sufficiently large implicit constant, the condition on $M$ in \cref{eq:main-predictive-sufficient-choices} implies both inequalities in \cref{eq:admissible-sampling-updates} and the preceding discretization requirement with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{disc}}=\varepsilon$.
This is a sufficient number of sampling steps, not a minimax lower bound for the number of reverse updates.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first verify approximation and covering for the deterministic class.
We then apply the score-learning inequality and transfer its error to the randomized sampler on the same training event.

The grid and floor choices give \cref{eq:accuracy-grid-size}.
Substitution of \cref{eq:accuracy-component-tolerances} into the definition of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net},n}$ gives $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net},n}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tar},n}/3$.
\Cref{lem:smooth-latent-explicit-tail-bounds,lem:smooth-latent-output-clipping} give
\begin{equation*}
 A R_{\mathrm{bal},n}^2\delta_{\mathrm{tail},n}
 +\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tail},n}^2
 +\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out,clip},n}^2
 +\varepsilon_{\mathrm{lab,clip}}^2(R_{\mathrm{lab},n})
 \lesssim\varepsilon^2.
\end{equation*}
In particular the output-clipping contribution is at most $2A\exp(-c_{\mathrm{lab}}^2 \log(e/\varepsilon)/2)=o(\varepsilon^2)$.
Applying \cref{prop:integrated-transformer-approximation} proves
\begin{equation*}
 {\mathcal{E}}_{\mathrm{app}}({\mathcal{S}}_{n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{lat}})\lesssim\varepsilon^2.
\end{equation*}

The quantitative size and sensitivity bounds in \cref{prop:smooth-latent-complexity} hold for arbitrary grids and component tolerances.
They therefore apply directly to the parameter choices made above for the integrated error.
Here $t_0^{-1}$, $T$, $R_{\mathrm{bal},n}$, the grid size, all inverse nonzero tolerances, and the prior-logit radius are polynomially bounded in $n$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$.
The local OU moduli and the numbers of components are likewise polynomial.
The fixed-depth attention sensitivity recursion and the clipped readout give polynomial parameter radius and parameter sensitivity over the entire class.
Consequently, using the bounds $B_{\mathrm{lat},n}$ and $\mathsf{Lip}_{\mathrm{lat},n}^{\mathrm{par}}$ from \cref{prop:smooth-latent-complexity}, evaluated at the choices above,
\begin{align}
 \logN_{\mathrm{cov}}(u,{\mathcal{S}}_{n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{lat}},d_{\mathrm{bal},\infty})
 &\le\mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{param},n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{lat}}
 \log\left(1+2B_{\mathrm{lat},n}\mathsf{Lip}_{\mathrm{lat},n}^{\mathrm{par}}/u\right),\nonumber\\
 \Gamma_{n,\varepsilon,\delta}
 &\lesssim\mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{param},n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{lat}}\log(en/\varepsilon)
       +\log(2/\delta).
 \label{eq:accuracy-cover-bound}
\end{align}
This establishes the approximation and complexity claims used in \cref{thm:main-generation-error-formal}.
The exact empirical minimizer exists measurably by the compactness and continuity argument in \cref{prop:smooth-latent-complexity}; the theorem permits any measurable approximate minimizer with the specified scaled-objective gap.

Apply \cref{thm:balanced-score-oracle} with its predictor radius $R_{\mathrm{pred}}=R_{\mathrm{out},n}$, the cover radius in \cref{eq:accuracy-component-tolerances}, and optimization tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}$.
With probability at least $1-\delta$, this gives \cref{eq:main-balanced-score-oracle}.
The uniform output bound and $t\ge t_0>0$ ensure that the learned score is finite-valued and Borel on the full state domain, as required by \cref{cor:randomized-grid-update-bound}.
In that corollary, $A/M\le1/2$ makes the shifted terminal-time error $\lesssim\varepsilon$ by \cref{eq:accuracy-diffusion-times}; the early-stopping error is at most $\varepsilon/4$.
Also $A\ge T-t_0$ and $M\ge2A$, so
\begin{equation*}
 \frac{A\sqrt{T-t_0}}{M}\le\frac{A}{\sqrt{M}}.
\end{equation*}
Taking square roots of \cref{eq:main-balanced-score-oracle} proves the main predictive bound.
                                                                                                                    
The task-conditional consequence is derived separately in \cref{cor:task-conditional-prompt-rate} by combining this predictive bound with \cref{eq:main-generation-error-decomposition}.
Finally $A\lesssim \log(e/\varepsilon)$ and $(R_{\mathrm{out},n}+R_{\mathrm{lab},n})^2\lesssim \log(e/\varepsilon)$ give the displayed logarithmic form.
The probability statement is for each model separately, with uniformly bounded failure probability and common deterministic constants.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $d_z=d_\theta=1$, $\beta=\beta'=\beta_\theta=1$, with sample-only prompts and $\delta=n^{-1}$.
In this paragraph $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}$ hides powers of $\log(en)$ only.
Let $t_{0,n}$ and $T_n$ denote the choices in \cref{eq:accuracy-diffusion-times} evaluated at $\varepsilon=\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$.
With $\varepsilon=\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$, the diffusion and radius choices give
\begin{equation*}
 t_{0,n}\asymp \log(en)/n,\qquad
 \sigma_{t_{0,n}}^{-1},R_{\mathrm{bal},n},R_{\mathrm{num},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}
 =\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^{1/2}),\qquad J_{\theta,n}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n).
\end{equation*}
The state, final-output, and label radii, $T_n$, and $A_{t_{0,n},T_n}$ are logarithmic in $n$.
Formula \cref{eq:accuracy-component-tolerances} gives
\begin{equation*}
 \varepsilon_{\ell,n}^{-1}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^2),\quad
 \varepsilon_{a,n}^{-1}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n),\quad
 \varepsilon_{b,n}^{-1}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^{1/2}),\quad
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rat},n}^{-1}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^{1/2}).
\end{equation*}
There are ${\mathcal{O}}(\log n)$ overlapping time patches.
On patches with $a_j\le1$, $h_j^{\mathrm{loc}}\le7a_j$ and $\sigma_{a_j}^2\asymp a_j$; on later patches, $\sigma_{a_j}^{-1}={\mathcal{O}}(1)$ and $h_j^{\mathrm{loc}}\le T_n$.
Since $H_{q,x}=0$, \cref{eq:smooth-latent-local-denominator-modulus,eq:smooth-latent-local-numerator-modulus} give
\begin{equation*}
 \max_j H_{a,j,n}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n),\qquad
 \max_j H_{b,j,n}=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^{3/2}).
\end{equation*}
The two-dimensional state--time basis size is therefore
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf{N}_{\mathrm{basis},n}^{\mathrm{lat}}
 =\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}\!\left(n\{(n\,n)^2+(n^{3/2}n^{1/2})^2\}\right)
 =\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^5).
\end{equation*}
The likelihood and fixed ratio module sizes are $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^3)$ and $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^2)$, respectively.
The token width is ${\mathcal{O}}(J_{\theta,n})$; the attention projection count is $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^2)$ and its forward cost is $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}((n+J_{\theta,n})J_{\theta,n}^2)=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^3)$.
Repeated likelihood evaluation costs $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^4)$.
Thus the basis term dominates the numbers of trainable parameters, stored coefficients, and forward-pass operations, each bounded by $\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^5)$.
Substitution into \cref{eq:main-predictive-sufficient-choices} with $\varepsilon=\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$ gives $N=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n^6)$ and $M=\widetilde{{\mathcal{O}}}(n)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
For the lower bound, we construct a hypercube of smooth densities, apply an Assouad testing argument~\citep{tsybakov2009introduction}, and embed the entire family into a one-dimensional latent path.

Choose a nonzero $\psi\in C_c^\infty((0,1))$ with $\int\psi=0$ and $\|\psi\|_\infty\le1$, extended by zero outside $(0,1)$.
Write $b_1=\int_0^1|\psi|>0$ and $b_2=\int_0^1\psi^2>0$.
For sufficiently large $n$, set
\begin{equation*}
 m=\left\lfloor\tfrac{1}{4}\log_2 n\right\rfloor\ge1,
 \qquad a=\kappa\sqrt{m/n},\qquad K=2^m,
\end{equation*}
where $\kappa>0$ is a fixed small constant chosen below.
For $v\in\{-1,1\}^m$, define
\begin{equation*}
 p_v(z)=1+a\sum_{j=1}^m v_j\psi(mz_1-j+1),
 \qquad z\in[0,1]^{d_z}.
\end{equation*}
The perturbations have disjoint supports and zero integral, so $p_v$ is a density with $1-a\le p_v\le1+a$.

We check spatial regularity under \cref{eq:holder-norm-convention}, including integer $\beta$.
Recall $m_{\beta}=\lceil\beta\rceil-1$ and $\vartheta_{\beta}=\beta-m_{\beta}\in(0,1]$ from Appendix~\ref{app:subsec:regularity-conventions}, and write $\widetilde{p}_v=(p_v-1)/a$.
Disjointness gives $\|\partial_1^s \widetilde{p}_v\|_\infty\le C_s m^s$ for every fixed integer $s\ge0$; derivatives involving other coordinates vanish.
The $m_{\beta}$th derivative has both a uniform bound $Cm^{m_{\beta}}$ and a Lipschitz bound $Cm^{m_{\beta}+1}$.
Thus
\begin{equation*}
 |\partial_1^{m_{\beta}}\widetilde{p}_v(z)-\partial_1^{m_{\beta}}\widetilde{p}_v(z')|
 \lesssim\min\{m^{m_{\beta}},m^{m_{\beta}+1}\|z-z'\|_2\}
 \le Cm^\beta\|z-z'\|_2^{\vartheta_{\beta}}.
\end{equation*}
Consequently $\|p_v\|_{C^\beta}\le1+C_{\beta,d_z,\psi}a m^\beta$.
Since $a m^\beta\to0$, all these densities satisfy the fixed spatial norm bound $L_\beta>1$ and lower density bound $\underline{p}<1$ for large $n$.

Let $P_v$ have density $p_v$, let ${\mathbb{E}}_v:={\mathbb{E}}_{P_v^{\otimes n}}$, and let $d_{\mathrm{H}}$ denote Hamming distance.
Direct integration gives
\begin{equation*}
 {\mathsf{TV}}(P_v,P_w)=\frac{a b_1}{m}d_{\mathrm{H}}(v,w),
 \qquad
 \mathrm{KL}(P_v^{\otimes n}\|P_w^{\otimes n})
 \le\frac{8na^2b_2}{m}=8\kappa^2b_2
 \quad\text{if }d_{\mathrm{H}}(v,w)=1.
\end{equation*}
For the KL bound, take $a\le1/2$ and use $\mathrm{KL}(P_v\|P_w)\le\int(p_v-p_w)^2/p_w$ on the single differing bump.
Choose $0<\kappa\le\min\{1,(8\sqrt{b_2})^{-1}\}$.
Pinsker's inequality then gives ${\mathsf{TV}}(P_v^{\otimes n},P_w^{\otimes n})\le1/2$ for neighboring vertices.

For any Borel probability-valued estimator $Q_D$, where $D=Z_{1:n}$, let $\widehat{v}(Q_D)$ be the lexicographically first minimizer of $w\mapsto{\mathsf{TV}}(Q_D,P_w)$.
This is measurable: TV from a fixed probability measure on the cube is a supremum over a countable generating algebra.
The definition of $\widehat{v}(Q_D)$ and the triangle inequality imply
\begin{equation*}
 {\mathsf{TV}}(Q_D,P_v)\ge\tfrac{1}{2}{\mathsf{TV}}(P_{\widehat{v}(Q_D)},P_v)
 =\frac{a b_1}{2m}d_{\mathrm{H}}(\widehat{v}(Q_D),v).
\end{equation*}
For each bit, pair the vertices that differ only in that bit.
The sum of the two testing-error probabilities in each pair is at least $1-{\mathsf{TV}}(P_v^{\otimes n},P_w^{\otimes n})\ge1/2$.
Averaging uniformly over all vertices therefore gives error probability at least $1/4$ for each bit.
Summing over the $m$ bits yields
\begin{equation*}
 2^{-m}\sum_v{\mathbb{E}}_v{\mathsf{TV}}(Q_D,P_v)
 \ge\frac{a b_1}{8}\gtrsim \sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{n}},
\end{equation*}
because $m\asymp\log(en)$.
The estimator need not have a density.
Randomized probability-valued estimators satisfy the same bound by averaging their output measures over the auxiliary randomization and using convexity of TV.

We next embed all $K=2^m$ densities into the fixed latent class.
Enumerate the vertices as $v^{(1)},\ldots,v^{(K)}$, put $\lambda_j=(j-1)/(K-1)$, and let $\bar p_\lambda$ interpolate linearly between $p_{v^{(j)}}$ and $p_{v^{(j+1)}}$ on each interval $[\lambda_j,\lambda_{j+1}]$.
Convexity preserves normalization, positivity, and the spatial norm.
Since $\|p_v-p_w\|_\infty\le2a$, summing the intervalwise Lipschitz bounds gives
\begin{equation*}
 \|\bar p_\lambda-\bar p_{\lambda'}\|_\infty\le2a(K-1)|\lambda-\lambda'|,
 \qquad
 2aK\le Cn^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation*}
For sufficiently large $n$, this Lipschitz constant is at most the fixed $H_\theta>0$.
Set $g_\theta(z)=\bar p_{\theta_1}(z)$ for $\theta\in[0,1]^{d_\theta}$.
This map is jointly Borel and satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \|g_\theta-g_{\theta'}\|_\infty
 \le H_\theta|\theta_1-\theta_1'|
 \le H_\theta|\theta_1-\theta_1'|^{\beta_\theta}
 \le H_\theta\|\theta-\theta'\|_2^{\beta_\theta},
\end{equation*}
using $|\theta_1-\theta_1'|\le1$.
Choose $\Pi_n=K^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^K\delta_{(\lambda_j,0,\ldots,0)}$.
The resulting environment belongs to $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{lat}}$ with all class bounds fixed, and its oracle risk is at least $c\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$ by the testing bound obtained above under the uniform prior on the vertices.
Although the hypercube has $m$ bits, its embedding uses only one latent coordinate.

For input--output prompts, set $g_\theta(x,z)=\bar p_{\theta_1}(z)$ on the unit input--output cube.
The same spatial and latent regularity checks apply.
The inputs, including $X_\star$, are uniform and independent of the task and output context.
Conditional on all these inputs, any kernel $Q(\cdot\mid C_n,X_\star)$ is an estimator based on the output context to which the preceding bound applies.
Averaging over the inputs gives the same lower bound.

Finally, fix the constructed environment $\mathcal{M}_n$.
For any rule using independent training episodes, write $\widehat Q_N^{\mathcal{M}_n}(\cdot\mid \mathsf d,h)$ for its output kernel given a training-data realization $\mathsf d$ and prompt $h$, and define the Borel kernel
\begin{equation*}
 \overline{Q}_h(A)
 :=\int \widehat Q_N^{\mathcal{M}_n}(A\mid \mathsf d,h)
 \mathsf{Law}_{\mathcal{M}_n}({\mathcal{D}}_N^{\mathrm{epi}})({\mathrm{d}} \mathsf d).
\end{equation*}
Independence of training from the fresh task and prompt, together with convexity of TV, shows that $\overline{Q}$ has no greater expected loss than the original rule.
The same construction applies to a countably infinite training sequence on its standard-Borel product space.
Hence independent pretraining cannot reduce the lower bound even when the entire environment is known.

label: cor:task-conditional-prompt-rate
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Task-conditional generation at the sharp prompt rate

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\varepsilon=\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$ and restrict to $n$ large enough that $\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$. Then $\log(e/\varepsilon)\lesssim\log(en)$ and $\log(en/\varepsilon)\lesssim\log(en)$. Applying \cref{thm:main-generation-error} and the covering bound in \cref{eq:accuracy-cover-bound} gives the posterior-predictive part of \cref{eq:main-smooth-latent-generation-rate}; \cref{eq:main-balanced-score-oracle} gives the stated score bound. The uniform upper bound in \cref{thm:main-task-uncertainty-and-minimax-rate} is $\lesssim\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$, so the triangle inequality gives the task-conditional bound on the same training event.

For the upper minimax bound, the score class chosen above and the fitting rule are common to all $\mathcal{M}\in\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{lat}}$.
Under each model, the conditional task risk is $\lesssim \sqrt{\log(en)/n}$ on an event of probability at least $1-n^{-1}$ and at most one otherwise.
Hence
\begin{equation*}
 {\mathbb{E}}_{\mathrm{train},\mathcal{M}}{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathcal{M}}{\mathsf{TV}}\!\bigl(\widehat{P}_{0\,|\,H_n}^{(M)},P(\cdot\mid H_n,\Theta)\bigr)
 \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{n}}+n^{-1}
 \lesssim\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{n}}.
\end{equation*}
The constants and sufficient choices are common, so taking the supremum over models preserves this bound.
The minimax infimum is no larger than the risk of this particular common rule.
Existence is ensured by the Borel exact ERM in \cref{prop:smooth-latent-complexity}; any common Borel fitting rule meeting the prescribed approximate-ERM tolerance satisfies the same upper bound.

For the lower bound, the construction in \cref{app:subsec:sharp-prompt-lower-bound} gives, for each sufficiently large $n$, one model in $\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{lat}}$ on which every probability-valued estimator has expected task risk at least $c\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$, even if given the model and independent training data.
This applies to every unknown-model learning rule in \cref{eq:latent-unknown-model-risk}.
Taking its supremum risk and then the infimum over rules proves the first inequality in \cref{eq:main-latent-minimax-sandwich}.
Averaging the predictive bound in the same way gives expected posterior-predictive TV $\lesssim \sqrt{\log(en)/n}$, without a matching $\sqrt{\log(en)/n}$ lower claim for that risk.
